summary: app/worker Docker healthchecks (Python-based, no curl/apt), caddy waits on app's condition: service_healthy instead of container-start; root-caused and fixed two latent defects surfaced while wiring this up: config had no Celery app (worker entrypoint would fail on boot) and the `redis` package kombu needs for the Valkey broker was never declared.

task_notes.RT-002: docker-compose.yml: app healthcheck hits /api/v1/health/ via `python -c urllib...` (no apt/curl needed); worker healthcheck is `celery -A config inspect ping`; caddy depends_on app uses condition: service_healthy. infra/api.Dockerfile: dropped the apt-get step (psycopg[binary] vendors libpq; ca-certificates already ships in python:3.12-slim), so the build needs no Debian mirror access. config/celery.py + config/__init__.py: standard Django/Celery app wiring (previously absent — `celery -A config worker` would have failed at startup). settings.py: CELERY_BROKER_URL/CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND from VALKEY_URL. pyproject.toml/uv.lock: added `redis` (kombu's redis transport hard-imports it; ImportError without it, reproduced locally).

escalations: Could not run `docker compose up --build` (full containerized boot) in this session: this sandbox's Docker daemon can reach container registries but not PyPI/npm from inside a build or a running container (apt-get and `pip install uv` both fail with DNS resolution errors; confirmed this is sandbox-wide, not specific to this Dockerfile). Verified the equivalent behavior instead by running the app/worker directly from the host venv against the same Postgres/Valkey images. RT-004 (cold-offline boot smoke) needs an environment where `docker compose up --build` can actually complete to be verified for real; flagging this to the owner before attempting it.
